newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metal wage talks break down in north German region.
newsitem.headline: Metal wage talks break down in north German region.

text.p: Wage talks covering 180,000 engineering workers in the northern German coastal region collapsed on Friday, prompting the IG Metall trade union to call temporary stoppages.
The failure of talks with employers after 14 hours contrasts with wage accords reached in most of the rest of Germany's giant engineering sector in the last two weeks.

The chief IG Metall negotiator for the region, Frank Teichmueller, said the negotiations had foundered on employer resistance to paying a supplement to sick pay for employees who were ill for more than six weeks.
The difference between the two sides' positions had been "fractional," Teichmueller said.
The chief negotiator for employers' association Nordmetall, Hans Werner Busch, described the union's stance as "totally unacceptable" as companies were unable to make further concessions.

IG Metall staged the first walk-outs on Friday with about 2,000 workers downing tools temporarily throughout the region, which spans the state of Schleswig-Holstein, the cities of Hamburg and Bremen and the northwestern part of Lower Saxony.

The engineering sector this week struck wage accords in the far larger regions of North Rhine-Westphalia and Bavaria which guaranteed full pay during sickness, in effect sealing the fate of plans to implement an unpopular law allowing 20 percent cuts in sick pay.
The deals set pay rises of 1.5 percent from April 1 next year and 2.5 percent from April 1998. Agreement was also reached for the southern part of the state of Baden-Wuerrtemberg.
Talks with employers had been deadlocked until a breakthrough was reached last week in the northern state of Lower Saxony, offering workers continued full sick pay and modest wage gains.

Teichmueller said IG Metall in the coastal region would agree to a deal that matched the Lower Saxony agreement and held out hope a deal may be reached in January. But if it did not, the union would call a strike.
Wage talks for western Berlin also ended without agreement but the IG Metall branch there said talks would resume on January 7.
